description:
FILED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5 CHECK 2.

t/run/cloexec.t is 26 blessed fail rows over ONE fact: perl's `$^F`
($SYSTEM_FD_MAX) decides which descriptors survive an `exec` -- a descriptor at
or below `$^F` is NOT marked FD_CLOEXEC and the exec'd child inherits it, above
it is.  The file opens a temp file, notes `fileno`, sets `$^F` above and below
it, and has a child `exec`'d program read the descriptor back.

MEASURED (s473t5d, `--jobs 1`): PCL's child reads ONE line where perl's reads
TWO --

  not ok 8  - child stdout: has 2 newlines      got 1, expected 2
  not ok 9  - child stdout: split into 2 lines  got 1, expected 2
  not ok 11 - child stdout: line 1              got undef

-- while the rows about the PARENT's own view (`parent open fd=5 ($^F=4)`,
`tmpfile ... exists`, `child stdout: fd`) all PASS.  So the parent side of the
model is right and the INHERITANCE is not.  The file also renumbers (PCL emits
11 extra TAP rows), which is why 11 of the 26 are `(none) -> extra`.

WHERE TO LOOK: PCL sets FD_CLOEXEC on the descriptors it opens (task #592 notes
the fdopen exception), and `$^F` is where perl's policy lives.  The open path
must consult `$^F` -- ONE reading, like `%p-output-buffering` is for buffering
-- rather than a fixed choice.  Probe the shape that would BREAK: PCL's own
internal descriptors (the saved core, the module cache, the sweep's own
plumbing) must stay close-on-exec whatever a program sets `$^F` to.

ROWS: 26 blessed fail rows (11 `ok -> (missing)`, 11 `extra`, the rest not ok);
no registered shortfall.
subject: a descriptor above $^F is not inherited across exec: t/run/cloexec.t's child sees one line where perl sees two
